item.title: OpenAI Releases Codex Security for Vulnerability Detection and Remediation
item.description:
OpenAI Releases Codex Security for Vulnerability Detection and Remediation

OpenAI has released Codex Security, a toolset for finding, investigating, and fixing vulnerabilities in code. It provides security workflows accessible in Codex, a command-line interface, and a TypeScript SDK for automation.

🔍 Overview

Codex Security helps developers:

  • Scan repositories, selected paths, or Git changes
  • Validate candidate findings, generate patches, and verify existing fixes
  • Draft SECURITY.md policies and save threat models for later review
  • Browse saved scans and findings, identify duplicates, assess severity against custom rubrics, and suggest owners from source and Git history
  • Preview third-party scanner findings, save them locally, or publish supported reports to Codex Security Cloud

🧩 How It Works

Scan Types

  • Standard scans investigate code for vulnerabilities
  • Deep scans repeat Standard scans and return deduplicated findings
  • Scans use existing root and component SECURITY.md guidance
  • A completed scan saves a report and findings

Post-Scan Actions

  • Read the report for source evidence and exclusions
  • Request a patch or ask Codex to verify an existing fix
  • Track findings in Linear, Jira, or GitHub
  • Export results as SARIF, JSON, or CSV

⚙️ Key Details

Installation & Requirements

Component Requirement
Node.js 22.13.0+ within 22.x, or 24.x, or 26.x
Python 3.10+ (Python 3.10 also requires tomli)

CLI Usage

  • cs and codex-security run the same CLI
  • Use npx @openai/codex-security to skip global install or resolve EEXIST conflicts
  • Run cs scan . --max-time 15 for a 15-minute Standard investigation allowance
  • Use bulk scans for independent repository reviews in one resumable campaign
  • When the scan completes, open the Markdown file at the REPORT path in the terminal
  • Run cs scans show from the same repository to find its latest completed scan

CI Configuration

  • Set OPENAI_API_KEY or CODEX_API_KEY in the scan process’s environment

🔗 Integrations & Automation

  • Automate scans across repositories or project components, including in CI and containers
  • Publish completed scans to Codex Security Cloud (optional; local scans work without it)
  • When Codex Security Cloud is available, the Security plugin’s $cloud-findings skill reads findings, reports, recorded assignment and verification, and scan status in Codex desktop or the Codex CLI
  • Linked Git worktrees share scan history and saved findings when they use the same Codex Security state directory
  • Keep CODEX_SECURITY_STATE_DIR stable to retain shared history and sign-in scope

🔐 Advanced Features & Access Programs

  • Some cybersecurity requests and protected findings require Trusted Access for Cyber
  • For accounts with Daybreak access:
    • See Daybreak opt-in for the Codex toggle
    • See Cyber access programs to select a program explicitly
  • The SDK guide includes deep-scan configuration, validation, severity classification, owner suggestions, and result handling
  • Use policy to draft a new SECURITY.md or update an existing one

item.title: ComfyUI-KJNodes Introduces Enhanced Set/Get Node Functionality
item.description:
ComfyUI-KJNodes Introduces Enhanced Set/Get Node Functionality

🔍 Overview

The ComfyUI-KJNodes project has recently undergone a significant update, introducing enhanced functionalities for Set/Get nodes within the ComfyUI framework. This update focuses on extending support to both legacy and nodes 2.0, alongside promoting cross-subgraph interconnectivity.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Backward Compatibility: The rewrite maintains compatibility with earlier versions, ensuring seamless integration with existing workflows.
  • Subgraph Functionality: Set/Get nodes now operate across parent and child subgraphs, facilitating broader interactions within multi-tiered structures.
  • New Operations:
    • Convert link to Set/Get using a right-click on any link midpoint.
    • Batch convert selected node outputs to Set/Get pairs.
    • The canvas right-click menu supports the conversion of outputs on selected nodes.
  • Key Shortcuts:
    • Ctrl+Shift+S: Add Set nodes.
    • Ctrl+Shift+G: Add Get nodes.
    • Ctrl+Shift+L: Toggle visibility of all connections.
  • Settings Enhancements: New settings for managing link visibility, keyboard shortcuts without conflicting with other actions, and sprite appearance based on connections.
  • Conversion Features: Right-clicking a SetNode adds a corresponding GetNode, and double-clicking a GetNode navigates to its paired SetNode.
  • Type and Color Update: Nodes now reflect type changes when inputs or outputs are disconnected, ensuring consistency in visual feedback.
  • Settings Structure: Settings have been reorganized under KJNodes > Set & Get and KJNodes > General categories for improved navigation.

💡 Why It Matters

This update enhances user interaction and workflow efficiency within the ComfyUI ecosystem. The integration of Set/Get functionalities across subgraphs and the addition of user-friendly features signifies an advancement in customization capabilities, empowering users to build more complex and interconnected AI pipelines.

🚀 Availability

To begin using these features, users should:

  1. Clone the custom_nodes repo to the custom_nodes folder.
  2. Install dependencies using pip install -r requirements.txt.

For portable installs, utilize:

1

custom_setup/ComfyUI_windows_portable-folder/python_embeded/python.exe -m pip install -r ComfyUI/custom_nodes/ComfyUI-KJNodes/requirements.txt

item.title: ClawGod: Runtime Patch for Privacy and Features in Claude Code
item.description:
ClawGod: Runtime Patch for Privacy and Features in Claude Code

ClawGod is a runtime patch applied to the official Claude Code. It is not a third-party client but a layer applied on top of the existing application that continues to be supported with each version update.

🔍 Overview

As Claude Code updates, ClawGod automatically re-extracts and re-patches against the new version on the next launch. This ensures compatibility with any version of the official tool. The patch is designed to enhance functionality and modify specific behaviors, such as enabling “God mode” and implementing privacy protections that are enabled by default.

🧩 How it works

The tool operates by modifying internal logic at runtime. A key aspect of its functionality is the neutralization of known location and proxy signals embedded in prompts. For instance, the “Date String” feature addresses a system prompt encoding where user location was inferred via Unicode apostrophe variants and date separators; ClawGod patches this to always use ASCII apostrophes and unmodified date formats. Additionally, the “Geo-Detection Probe” is patched to always return null, preventing client-side detection based on timezone, proxy hostnames, or vendor keywords.

⚙️ Key details

ClawGod introduces a wide range of features and overrides, including:

  • Internal User Mode: Access to 24+ hidden commands (e.g., /share, /teleport, /issue), debug logging, and API request dumps.
  • GrowthBook Overrides: The ability to override any feature flag via a config file.
  • Agent Teams: Multi-agent swarm collaboration without requiring flags.
  • Computer Use: Screen control on macOS without a Max/Pro subscription.
  • Auto-mode: Unlocks auto-mode for third-party API users by removing the firstParty gate.
  • Classifier Tuning: Tunable parameters for the auto-mode classifier, including timeout, model, and retries.
  • Ultraplan & Ultrareview: Multi-agent planning and automated bug hunting via Claude Code Remote.

🛡️ Privacy and Security

Since v2.3.0, ClawGod blocks the automatic collection of Git origin and environment metadata for the x-claude-code-wiggly-dove header. The patch ensures the shared eligibility gate returns false before the collector runs, preventing the reading of Git origin or other environment metadata. Other security features include:

  • CYBER_RISK_INSTRUCTION: Refusal mechanisms for security testing and exploits.
  • URL Restriction: Instructions to never generate or guess URLs.
  • Cautious Actions: Forced confirmation before destructive operations.
  • Enterprise Remote Settings: Organization-managed settings for forced permission rules and version pinning, which can be disabled via CLAWGOD_FEATURE_REMOTE_SETTINGS=false.

🚀 Availability

ClawGod is available via installation scripts for different operating systems:

  • Linux/macOS: curl -fsSL https://github.com/0Chencc/clawgod/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
  • Windows: irm https://github.com/0Chencc/clawgod/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex
